label: copy phase, near an output of k (also 2/v/w/n)
predicate: (phase == 2) & ((out_tok == tok("k")) | (next_out == tok("k")) | (out_at(-1) == tok("k")) | (out_at(-2) == tok("k")) | isin(out_tok, [tok(c) for c in "2vwn"]))
explanation: Copy-phase feature: 97% of activation mass falls at t > L, and it almost never fires in the original phase or on the <DEL> step. Inside the copy phase it is graded by token, centred on the letter k. It fires on 89% of steps that output k, and the strongest activations are on runs of k (top examples: x i k k k v v -> peak on the output of the first k, then decaying over the following k outputs). It is also elevated one step before a k output (next_out k, 56%) and one or two steps after one. Weaker preferred outputs are 2, v, w and n (about 30-40% rate), and other tokens give low-level activations (rate about 10-20%). Magnitude is highest on k outputs and decays with distance from the k. Rate rises over recall_idx 1-4. A k-window plus {2,v,w,n} predicate reaches about 0.59 F1 and 0.76 mass recall on dev. The remaining low-magnitude firing is spread over many other copy-phase tokens.
